A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ACES system. Their text, figures, tables, and included appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including the original computational study and v3's added Appendix B.

before.justification: Section 4.1 and Table 2 report original cohort sizes, runtimes, and memory measurements for nine extraction tasks on MIMIC-IV.

after.justification: Section 3.1 and Table 2 retain those original measurements. Appendix B additionally reports experiments comparing ACES with DPM360 and OMOP-learn.

M1.justification: The dataset-specific predicates, dataset-agnostic windows, supported input formats, and recursive extraction approach are retained. Section 2.1 and Figure 3 in v3 explain the existing algorithm more fully; they do not establish a changed extraction procedure.

E1.justification: The nine MIMIC-IV tasks remain. Appendix B broadens evaluated data to 1,000 Synthea-generated patients and uses a MIMIC-IV Demo subset. It also includes an end-of-life prediction entry, although its detailed task requirements are unspecified. Coverage remains clinical cohort extraction.

E2.justification: V2 reports ACES profiling without evaluated competitors. Table B.1 adds DPM360 comparisons on Synthea-1000 and OMOP-learn comparisons on MIMIC-IV Demo, each across four tasks. ATLAS and PIC-SURE are discussed but are not separately benchmarked.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces a comparative protocol measuring runtime, peak memory, code length including configuration/template code, and human time. It evaluates ACES through MEDS and competitors through OMOP on an A100 instance with 84 GB RAM and 12 CPU cores. The original single-shard, 36-core/340-GB profiling protocol is retained.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or error analyses. Appendix B adds benchmark comparisons; its discussion of adapting configurations versus SQL/Python changes does not provide a separate tested adaptation analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point measurements without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new comparative table does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All 36 numerical result cells in Table 2 are unchanged. Table B.1 adds substantial comparative results: for first-24-hour hospital mortality on MIMIC-IV Demo, runtime is 0.617 seconds for ACES versus 12.220 for OMOP-learn. Memory advantages are not universal: Synthea end-of-life extraction uses 421 MiB for ACES versus 387 for DPM360. These are new comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. V3 expands the informal explanation of recursive window extraction without introducing new mathematical assumptions, derivations, or formal properties.

C1.justification: The central reproducibility, interoperability, and accessible cohort-extraction claims remain. The third enumerated contribution changes from anticipated field-wide reproducibility benefits to an explicit novelty claim for a DSL using event-bounded query aggregations to improve expressiveness and efficiency.

C2.justification: Appendix B interprets the comparisons as workflow and adaptability benefits while explicitly acknowledging possible bias from greater familiarity with ACES. The roadmap extends prospective unstructured-data support to images and replaces v2's claim of promising preliminary LLM results with a future-work proposal.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies the original shard's 47,954 patients, 80,301,208 rows, and disk/in-memory sizes, and documents hardware and data formats for Appendix B. These disclosures do not establish changes to the original experiment. Repository and documentation pointers remain; the video pointer disappears and Table 1's snippet link targets change, with their contents unavailable in the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: V3 adds an explicit connection to Donoho's frictionless reproducibility, expands discussion of PIC-SURE and DPM360, and discusses MEDS-DEV in the main text after v2 had linked it in Appendix A. Additional references support these connections and Synthea usage. The underlying positioning against CDM-specific tools remains.

P1.justification: The methods narrative is substantially reorganized: former Section 3's technical-design material is replaced by an expanded algorithm subsection within Section 2, preceding configuration and interface details. API/output subsections are reordered, separate video and reproducibility sections disappear, and prose throughout the main text and documentation index is revised.

P2.justification: V3 adds workflow Figure 1, recursive-algorithm Figure 3, and comparative Table B.1. V2's Figures 1 and 2 survive as Figures 2 and 4. Its detailed sample-output Figure 3 is removed, although the new workflow includes a compact output example. These changes substantially revise the visual explanation.

improvement.justification: V3 improves assessability through the first direct comparator measurements, clearer algorithm explanations and diagrams, and precise workload details. However, Appendix B remains preliminary: evaluation is restricted to synthetic/demo data, evaluator-familiarity bias is acknowledged, and uncertainty is unreported. The loss of the detailed output illustration and video pointer offsets some explanatory gains. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
